A puzzle box is an item occasionally received during a hard or elite Treasure Trail when completing hard anagram or cryptic clues. Players need to complete the puzzle in order to receive their next clue. They are similar to the real world wp | sliding puzzle .

Puzzle boxes contain a scrambled image that players must work to unscramble by clicking on tiles to move them to an empty space. Once the puzzle box is completed, players need to talk to the NPC who gave them puzzle to receive the next clue or the reward. In elite trails, solving the puzzle automatically presents the player with the next clue or the reward upon closing the window. Destroying a puzzle box does not reset the progress, and is restored upon re-obtaining the box. While puzzle boxes from compass clues are random, NPCs give the same puzzle box each time; for example, Oziach will always give the Vanstrom Klause puzzle, while Zenesha will always give the Wizard puzzle.

For accessibility to players with arachnophobia, puzzle boxes bearing an image of Araxxor have a unique "Flip" option when right-clicked; this will replace the image of a spider with another image. Progress will not be lost and the flipped puzzle will have the same solution.

Puzzle boxes have a 'hint' in the bottom left hand corner that shows the player the image of the completed puzzle.

All puzzles can be found on free-to-play worlds, though some puzzles will be unsolvable, thus preventing the players from obtaining access to some rooms. Puzzles only appear when Complexity is set to High.

Skill-based puzzles have their skill requirements capped to the party's level, so they will always be solvable by at least one person in the party as long as all the original members are present.

Transferable resources

A list of puzzles with one or more transferable resources:
• Fishing ferret - vile fish
• Hunter ferret - traps
• Three statue weapon, and ten statue weapon - stone block
• Magic construct - lump of stone
• Grapple tightrope, and winch room - broken climbing hook head, meatcorn
• Keystone bridge - carved keystone
• Coloured recess - blue vial, green vial, yellow vial, and violet vial
• Broken plank bridge - wooden plank

The level requirements to process resources may vary between different iterations of the same room in the same dungeon, so if you can't, for example, cook vile fish for one ferret room, you might still be able to cook the fish from another ferret room and then bring the fish back to the one you couldn't solve before.

Icy pressure pad

Overview

The floor is covered in a sheet of ice, along with 4 squares. To complete the puzzle, players will have to land on each of the 4 squares.

This puzzle only appears on frozen floors. It is solvable in free-to-play worlds.

Solution

The solution varies each time. Though there is no official solution (there are different puzzles) the best tactic to use is to eye yourself on an obstacle or pad, and then angle each way. You can move diagonally. Clicking on the eight squares around your player instead of on the destination will help reduce errors. You will stop if you are near an obstacle (3x3 range of the obstacle itself) or hit a tile.

If you have branches of any kind, it might be useful to light a fire to offset yourself from the corner.

Players who have the Gorajan trailblazer outfits will not slide across the ice and can simply run to each tile.

There is currently a bug such that a player owning the outfit can simply open the doors. This does not use the team's skip for that dungeon.

Seeker sentinel

Overview

In this room, a seeker sentinel rotates around in a circle with 4 seeker spawns patrolling and taking large breaks at certain points. The objective of this puzzle is reach another door and/or pick a key to progress through the dungeon. If a seeker spawn spots you, they will respond with a message appearing over their head, and the seeker sentinel will look your way. If you are spotted, you will receive damage and be teleported behind one of the stone walls.

This puzzle only appears on abandoned floors. It is solvable in free-to-play worlds.

Solution

The method to get around this room is to "subdue" the seeker spawn when they are facing away from you, with the seeker sentinel facing away from you too. When subdued, you can run past the seeker spawn, into the next alcove. Continue this method until you reach the door which you need to enter. Getting caught and being teleported on purpose can also be useful for progressing through the puzzle, as you are sometimes teleported next to the door. The damage dealt by the seeker sentinel is also less than many puzzles.

Sleeping guards

Overview

In this room, there are 4 sleeping brute guards and each of them has a key that can possibly unlock a door.

This puzzle only appears on furnished floors. It is solvable in free-to-play worlds.

Thieving helps, but not necessarily required

Solution

You must get the right key to unlock the door(s), this can be done in 2 ways.

The first (and recommended) method is to pickpocket the guards for the keys to unlock the doors in the room, taking care to walk, not run, over the broken glass. Pickpocketing can fail, in which ca

A lockbox is an item that is dug from the ground using a spade in front of the plaque at the Phoenix Gang Hideout in Varrock. It is found along with a note. Players must have the dry note (and at least 2 free inventory spaces) in their backpack when digging, otherwise nothing will be found.

Although the item offers an "Open" option that displays a combination lock interface, this interfaces proves to be a wp | red herring and serves no purpose other than to distract players from the correct method of progressing the Mod Sponge trading sequence. The instruction "use the passcode" in the note found alongside the lockbox is meant literally; using a dust rune on the lockbox will dissolve it, leaving behind another note when doing so. This does not consume the dust rune.

A double agent appears when doing a hard or master clue scroll. He says "I expect you to die!" when he appears and instantly attacks the player. His appearance is identical to Uri's.

He is also present in the You Are It quest, where he takes on his normal form, as well as a Ripper demon form, while still wearing his hat. In the quest, it is revealed that the double agent and Uri are the same person. Uri used a wishbringer made by Charos to wish for a vast hidden wealth, but he was also cursed to forever guard it as the double agent. Uri is able to take control of his body for short periods of time so he can help people find his treasures and save him, but the double agent then usually takes over.

Locations
• Hard and Master emote clues throughout the world:
• Double agents for hard clues in the Wilderness have a combat level of 77.
• Double agents for hard clues outside the Wilderness have a combat level of 98.
• Double agents for master clues have a combat level of 112 and 25,000 health.
• During the You Are It quest:
• McGrubor's Wood
• Lumbridge castle, in Duke Horacio's room
• Charos' tomb

Sextant.text:
A sextant is an essential item for solving coordinate clues on Treasure Trails. 

A sextant can be found on the tool belt. Players still need to talk to the Observatory professor about coordinate clues.

To use a sextant in the tool belt, choose the "sextant" option on a coordinate clue scroll or the "Look through" option sextant on the tool belt interface.

A sextant can be made by using one steel bar with level 23 Crafting on a Clockmaker's bench 4 in a player-owned house. Making a sextant gives 30 Crafting experience.

A sextant is used in conjunction with a watch when solving coordinate clues.

Creation

Disassembly

Disassembly
level: 1
category: default

Development history

Operating

Operating the sextant was a fairly simple task. The idea was to put the horizon and the sun in the middle of the screen.

Players need to use the vertical 'arrow buttons' on the right to put the horizon in the centre of the viewer on the right hand side. Then they need to use the horizontal arrow buttons to move the sun onto the horizon in the middle of the screen. Clicking 'get location' would give the coordinates of the player's position. This consisted of two numbers; the first indicated how far the player was north or south of the Observatory, in degrees and minutes, and the second how far east or west. One degree was 60 minutes, and each game square was approximately 1.875 minutes.

Sextants would often need to be used quickly in the Wilderness locations, as monster attacks could interrupt plotting.

Meerkats.text:
A meerkats is a forager familiar summoned by a meerkats pouch. It requires level 4 Summoning to summon. It is primarily used in Treasure Trails.

The familiar has the following abilities:
• Dig at the summoner's location.
• Increases scan clues range by 5 game squares.
• Provide sextant coordinates.

The familiar can cast the special move by consuming a Meerkat scroll (Fetch Casket), which digs for a coordinate, compass or scan clue without causing a Saradomin, Guthix, Zamorak wizard, Cabbagemancer, Bandosian wild mage, and Armadylean shaman to appear.

The meerkats pouches are received as a reward from a Treasure Trail and may not be made by players.

Hidey-hole.text:
Hidey-holes are storage units used to store items used in emote Treasure Trails clues. There are a total of 58 hidey-holes. They can be filled while the items are still equipped. There are achievements for building at least 1 hidey-hole as well as for completing all hidey holes.

Players can see which hidey-holes they've built or filled using the Treasure Trail information board near Zaida, or via a right-click option on the Treasure Trail collection log.

Materials

The materials and level required to convert these inconspicuous objects into hidey-holes depend on the tier of clue scroll they relate to. Despite the message saying steel nails are required, any type of nails can be used. However, all 10 nails must be of the same type. (Costs in the table below assume steel nails are used; cost will vary if using another type.) Visible boosts can be used to reach the Construction level requirements, but invisible boosts cannot. The Assist System cannot be used to build hidey-holes.

Clue scroll.text:
Clue scrolls are items that contain a step of Treasure Trails, a series of clues leading towards a reward casket.

There are different levels of clue scrolls, including easy, medium, hard, elite, and master, each with progressively harder clues and better rewards. The rewards can include valuable items, equipment, and cosmetic items. 

A new, sixth tier of clue scrolls, Grandmaster clue scrolls, was announced at RuneFest 2026. No release date was given, but they are planned to release as part of the first arc: Hoard of Dragons in Spring 2027.

They are received as sealed clue scrolls initially, that are drops from various monsters, skilling, or as rewards from completing quests.

When the players receive sealed clue scrolls, they can open one of them to convert to a clue scroll, read the clue scroll, and solve the clue on it in order to find a hidden treasure. These clues may involve various activities such as combat and puzzle solving, and may lead the player to various places.

After completing Desperate Times, a player will receive Charos' clue carrier, making it easier to store and transport sealed clue scrolls; saving bank space.

Sealed clue scrolls have a soft cap of 25 per tier (excluding master), which can be uncapped by purchasing the "Clue capacity removal" reward in the Treasure Trails Reward Shop. The soft cap means that players can obtain up to 25 of each tier, after which players will not receive any more unless it is from a guaranteed source (for example, skeletal horror). This cap includes both sealed clue scrolls as well as opened clue scrolls. If a player reaches this cap, and has a luck effect when rolling for (and missing out on) a clue scroll drop, the associated luck message will still be displayed.

Difficulty

There are five levels of clue scroll difficulties, with better rewards available as the difficulty increases. After the players complete the last clue of the set, they will receive a reward casket of corresponding difficulty.
